President Wilson's speech of Tuesday before the senate, therefore, is more than an academic discussion of the question of whether the United States should enter world peace league; it is an attempt to reopen the peace negotiations, or rather to further them, for they have never been closed.

The Monroe doctrine declares against European aggression on this continent, the Wilson doctrine declares against aggression anywhere.

destruction, may postpone the end,
but they cannot save the species in
the end.-Macon Telegraph.

Article I.- The name of this corporation shall be STATE OF LOUISIANA VINCE DE...

Article II.- The objects and purposes for which this corporation is formed are: to engage in the business of and to deal in chemicals and fertilizers of every kind and shape, to manufacture and deal in all kinds and, in certain cases, to attend to the handling of fluids and the absorption of gases; to acquire patents, by purchase or otherwise, for chemical processes and to operate and to acquire a patent applying to such material in the business of making sugar and all things necessary or convenient for the conduct of said business.

Article III.- The capital stock of this corporation shall be one hundred thousand dollars, also divided into one thousand shares, the par value of one hundred dollars each; the amount of each share to be paid in accordance with law.

Article IV.- The capital stock may be increased to two hundred thousand dollars, in such increments of five hundred dollars as may be required, by such officers as may be elected at the annual meeting of stockholders or at special meetings of stockholders.

Article V.- The business of the corporation shall be conducted by a Board of Directors, and the stockholders shall elect one President, one Secretary, and one Treasurer, and such other officers as may be necessary for the conduct of the business.

Article VI.- The Board of Directors may be divided into several classes, and the officers may be chosen from among the directors or from any other persons, and may hold such offices for such terms as may be fixed by the Board of Directors.

Article VII.- The Board of Directors may adopt, amend, or repeal by rule, and regulations for the business and all other matters as may be requisite and necessary.

Article VIII.- The Board of Directors shall have all the powers and authorities of a corporation, including the power to borrow money, to issue notes, to purchase and sell money, to employ such officers and agents as the corporation may require and to fix their compensation; to name directors as vacancies arise, and to make and enforce by rule, and regulations for the business and all other matters as may be requisite and necessary.

Article IX.- The Board of Directors shall have the power to make and issue stock, and to manage and control the business and affairs of the corporation, and to do all such other acts and things as may be necessary or convenient for the conduct of said business.

Article X.- The capital stock shall ever be held as the property of the corporation, and no part of the assets or property, real or personal, owned by the corporation shall be owned by any member of the organization, nor shall any member of the organization have any interest in the corporation, except as provided in this charter, nor shall any member of the organization be exposed to any liability for the debts or obligations of the corporation.

Article XI.- The Board of Directors shall hold meetings at any place as they may determine, and such meetings may be held at any time.

Article XII.- The election of successors in office shall take place as soon as possible after the election of the first directors, unless sooner dissolved, and the assets and property, real and personal, of the corporation shall be liquidated in such manner as the Board of Directors may determine.

PANS, Dec. The creation of an Interallied board to control sea transport and the feeding of the Allies is considered the solution of one of the most important questions dealt with by the Interallied Conference.

The delegates came here with the realization that unless the necessary tonnage could be found plans regarding the transportation &c foodstuffs and munitions to the troops could not be carried out according to programme.

Messrs. McCormick, Crosby, Perkins and Colby pointed out to their European colleagues that it was useless to arrange for the purchase of supplies and obtain the money to pay for them unless there were means to get these supplies where they are needed. To this extent the economic work of the conference depended largely on the success which Mr. Colby and his associates achieved in assembling and coordinating the shipping facilities of the Entente in common programme.

No Waste Tonnage.
By this method there will be no waste of tonnage. Shipments will be regulated so that precedence will be given to the commodity most needed, which will go where the demand for it is greatest. To make this programme effective all available ships will be driven from now on to their utmost capacity in speed for the transportation of material and men, the idea being to work the present tonnage to the maximum until the situation is relieved by new construction in England and the first ships are furnished by the United States under her building programme.

Some help will come from Japan and also from the German ships sailed to South America, but France and Italy will be unable to furnish any additional tonnage. A pool will be formed of all ships available, which will be apportioned according to the necessities of the different Entente nations and the amount and nature of the commodities which the United States can spare for them at the moment.

The board also will endeavor to free as much tonnage as possible for the transportation of American troops, not losing sight of the fact that their supplies and war material for the most part must precede them to France. The amount of material to be transported during the coming winter also will be increased by extensive improvements made in certain French ports by the installation of new docks and up to date unloading machinery, which will cut in half the time required to discharge cargo.

American Delegates Praised.
The efficiency of the American delegates is the subject of most eulogistic comment in the French papers, which agree that the expeditious work of the conference is largely due to their experience and methods. The journal says:

"The participation of the United States in the interallied conference produced remarkable results in the way of methodical organization. We have seen the creation of a common war treasury, the standardization and increase of naval construction, common control of sea transportation, determination of means for fighting submarines, plans for the concentration and distribution of food products, definition of the scope of the economic blockade and unity of naval control, all blocked out by various committees, submitted to the conference and approved in the shortest space of time."

Col. House has expressed himself on several occasions as proud of the efficient work of his associates, who, he said, stripped the husks from the problems they handled and presented only the kernels to the conference in the shape of logical, concrete recommendations.

Governor Burnquist has acted wisely formally forbidding the holding of the convention of the Peoples Peace Council which scheduled to open sessions here yesterday. It is almost a foregone conclusion that if the convention was insisted by its proponents there would be popular outbursts of violence against them that would lead to violence and bloodshed.
